newsitem.title: MACAU: China and Macau police confer as triad war rages.
newsitem.headline: China and Macau police confer as triad war rages.

text.p: Chinese police arrived on Monday for discussions with Macau police as the Portuguese-ruled enclave worked on a strategy to tackle violent turf wars between rival "triad" gansters.

Zheng Shaodong, head of the seven-member police group from the adjacent Chinese province of Guangdong, told reporters the two sides would discuss "matters of mutual interest" but he declined to go into detail.
The meeting coincides with a surge in violent crime in Macau, which has recorded 14 gang-related murders so far this year versus 21 for the whole of last year.
Macau, a territory of 455,000 on the south China coast, has been under Portuguese rule for four and a half centuries and is set to return to Beijing's control in 1999.
Police suspect many of the shootings, often performed by motorcylists, were carried out by imported mainland hitmen.
Triad brotherhoods, often with links in China, are believed to be fighting over illegal business linked to Macau's legal casino industry, such as protection rackets.
Macau officials are cautious when talking about Chinese police help or intervention to help stop the wave of violence.

A spokesman for Macau's criminal investigations department, the Judicial Police, told Reuters its director, Antonio Marques Baptista, recently visited Portugal to hire several police experts to help battle organised crime.
A senior source in the Judicial Police said he expected detectives specialising in fighting organised crime would be sent from Portugal to Macau within the next few weeks.
